name: Nested multi-notch phaser techniques for pads: grouped notches (groups × notches-per-group), pinch spacing, slow pinch 'breathing', stepped cutoff wah→flanger, scale-quantized random cutoff, slow triangle-swept full-depth bed
goal: Use a dense, nested phaser (notches arranged in up to ~6 groups × ~11 notches, one cutoff sliding all of them, resonance = notch width, depth = intensity, pinch = squeeze/spread within each group) as a cinematic pad mover: metallic shimmer layer (4 groups, 9 notches, depth ~82, raise pinch), inside-out 'tubular' breathing (pinch modulated by a slow quarter-note-synced LFO, depth ~63, try 2 vs 4 groups), static 'radio' sculpt (1 group, 1 notch, depth ~72), 1/16 stepped cutoff that turns from wah (1 notch) into flanger-like (7–9 notches) with glide, formant-like vowel push by slowly lowering cutoff (4/7, depth 65, low resonance), scale-quantized random cutoff (1/16, minor pentatonic, ~7 octave range) that stays in tune, and a slow breathing bed (6 groups, 11 notches, depth 100%, triangle sweep with ~10% glide).

source.title: You’ve Never Heard a Phaser Sound Like This

prerequisites: A phaser with many notches and per-group spacing — or build one: several cascaded all-pass chains whose notch frequencies are distributed in groups (Web Audio: many BiquadFilter(type='allpass') nodes with computed frequencies summed with dry; implementation note)
LFO, step sequencer with glide, random modulator with scale quantize

inputs.name: pad
inputs.description: Pad, guitar or vocal to process

outputs.name: phased_pad
outputs.description: Pad with shimmer, breathing or tuned-random spectral motion

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Source is a sponsored demo of one plugin algorithm; group/notch/pinch are generic aliases — any many-stage phaser or custom all-pass network can approximate it; no presets copied.
Settings are the presenter's display values; tune by ear.
Too many groups → mud; start around 4.

steps.action: Map the controls: groups ('nests'), notches per group ('peaks'), cutoff (moves all notches), resonance (notch width), depth (0 transparent → full phaser), pinch (squeeze/spread notches within each group).
steps.expect: Understanding of how each control moves the notch pattern

steps.action: Shimmer layer on a pad: 4 groups, 9 notches, depth ~82; slowly raise pinch until a metallic bell-like shimmer appears without taking over.
steps.expect: Shimmer that sits between granular and shimmer reverb

steps.action: Tubular breathing: same density (4/9), depth ~63; modulate pinch with a slow LFO synced to ~1/4 note. Compare 4 groups vs 2 groups — same motion, different character.
steps.expect: Notches squeeze/expand inside each group instead of sweeping left-right

steps.action: Static sculpt: 1 group, 1 notch, depth ~72 for a radio/telephone colour; move the notch up for 'pickup switch' tones; add groups to smooth it.
Stepped wah→flanger: 1/16-synced sequencer on cutoff at ~40–50% amount, 1 notch (wah); raise to 7–9 notches for a flanger-like texture; add glide so steps don't snap.
steps.expect: Rhythmic spectral movement that tracks the groove

steps.action: Vowel push on vocal-like material: 4 groups, 7 notches, depth 65, resonance low (~4), slowly lower cutoff.
Tuned random: random modulator on cutoff at ~1/16, quantized to a scale (e.g. minor pentatonic), range ~7.2 octaves. Change the scale to change the mood.
steps.expect: Jumping notches that still sound in key

steps.action: Breathing bed under a pad: 6 groups, 11 notches (maximum density), depth 100%, cutoff swept by a slow triangle sequence (rate ~2) with ~10% glide; then vary pattern, pinch and depth.
steps.expect: Deep, slow breathing movement under the pad

verification: Shimmer setting audibly adds high metallic content vs bypass without obvious sweep.
Pinch-LFO setting has motion with no obvious left-to-right sweep.
Scale-quantized random stays consonant over 30 s on a sustained chord.
